title: control-runbook-fragments-and-threat-stitch-marisol-2026
content:
Purpose: quick, messy brain-dump for mapping runtime security controls to collector evidence for SOC2 prep. Not an official artifact — use to draft the evidence pack and then move cleaned sections to Confluence.

Notes to self:
- Start with high-risk surfaces: auth, key management, data-at-rest, control plane access.
- Evidence types we can produce quickly: audit logs (cloud provider + app), KMS rotation records, IAM role change history, deployment pipeline approvals, runbooks with on-call rota.

Control stitching (rough):
- Logical access (CC6.x-ish): SSO (Okta) + SCIM sync logs + group membership export (monthly). Evidence = SCIM audit CSV + last 3 Okta admin action events.
- Crypto / KMS: Key rotation schedule (policy doc) + KMS audit log showing rotation events (last 12 months) + KMS IAM bindings. Need to confirm HSM vs cloud KMS in private clusters.
- Change management: GitHub protected branches + PR approvals + CI gate logs. Evidence = PR history export for sample set (last 30 PRs) + release notes.
- Logging & monitoring: Fluentd -> centralized ELK; retention 365d for security indices. Evidence = current retention setting screenshot + sample alert runbook and pagerduty escalation history.

Sampling approach idea:
- For each control pick 3–5 representative artifacts across last 6 months. One automated export (script) to gather: OKTA group exports, KMS admin logs, GitHub PR export, CloudTrail filtered events.
- Document sampling rationale in evidence index (why those items show control operating effectively).

Open questions / blockers:
1) Private deployment customers: do we include private-onprem KMS telemetry? (need input from eng-private-deployments). Ticketed: JIRA-TSK-2381.
2) Are retained logs stored in a separate account? If yes, do we need cross-account access proof? (ask infra)
3) How to present continuous batching as a ‘‘change’’ for config drift control? Might be operational config; propose a snapshot + hash approach.

Commands / quick exports to try (notes for scripter):
- Okta: export group members via API v1 -> filter for admin groups
- GCP/AWS: cloudtrail/aws logs -> aws cloudtrail lookup-events --start-time 2025-09-01 ...
- GitHub: gh api repos/redwood-inference/pulls --jq '.[] | {number,title,merged_by,merged_at,labels}' > sample_prs.json

Draft runbook fragment (for auditor show-and-tell):
- Incident triage: detect -> ack -> stabilize -> RCA timeline
- Evidence: pagerduty incident export + timeline from case ID -> attach slack thread and runbook step ids
- Postmortem: link to PM doc (template) + owner signature

Action items (short):
- [ ] Pull Okta admin events export for last 12 months (assigned Evan)
- [ ] Confirm log retention account and get read-only export creds (assigned Priya)
- [ ] Draft evidence index skeleton and circulate to Eng/SRE (me)
- [ ] Create sampling script stub and commit to trust-ops/tools (follow-on)

Meeting notes to include when drafting final:
- Auditors will ask for 'how do you prove continuous compliance' — prepare a narrative: automated exports + monthly control review + anomaly alerts.
- Keep a list of compensating controls for any private-deploy differences.

Random thoughts / short-term hacks:
- If missing KMS rotation logs: use key age metadata + ops tickets as supplemental evidence.
- For long-lived service accounts: produce a table with last-used timestamp (cloud SDK query) and owners.

Last reminders:
- Keep this doc ephemeral. Move polished lists and final evidence index to shared_drives/company/misc/trust-evidence when ready.
- Save exports under path: s3://redwood-trust-evidence/marisol/soctemp/YYYYMM

End of page.
